notes: ROS 1 package (catkin, package.xml format 1, yaml-cpp 0.3 API: GetNextDocument/FindValue). QoS is null for ROS 1; queue sizes: output 10 (nodelet.cpp:131), each input 10 (nodelet.cpp:150), and a latched std_msgs/String topic 'active' with queue 1 (nodelet.cpp:84) that is not a packet element. Output topic name: code default is 'output' on the private handle, i.e. cmd_vel_mux/output when the nodelet is named cmd_vel_mux as in example.launch; the optional YAML key 'publisher' overrides it (nodelet.cpp:127-130), and param/example.yaml:42 sets 'output/cmd_vel' while param/reconfigure.yaml has no publisher key (so the default 'output' applies). The output republishes each allowed input message unchanged (nodelet.cpp:53); Twist has no header and the code sets no frame, so frame is null; the Twist/Vector3 definitions state no units. topic:cmd_vel_mux/auto_docking: the package subscribes only to topic names read at run time from the YAML 'subscribers' list (cmd_vel_subscribers.cpp:30; nodelet.cpp:147-150); 'auto_docking' (and 'dock' in any form) appears nowhere in the snapshot, including both shipped YAML files (example.yaml lists input/default, input/navigation, input/joystick, input/remote, input/webapp, input/keyop; reconfigure.yaml lists input/default, input/navigation, input/safety), so it is in neither references nor not_declared. Its port msg_type comes from the generic subscription mechanism; its timeout and priority would come from that external YAML. yaml_cfg_file: packet side is consumes; it is read with getParam when the dynamic_reconfigure value is empty (nodelet.cpp:99-103) and is also declared as a string dynamic_reconfigure parameter with default "" (reload.cfg:9) served on the private node handle (nodelet.cpp:81); a missing file is logged and the reload is skipped (nodelet.cpp:113-117).
